title: Performance budgets and service profiles for model endpoints
author: Marco Chen
content:
Summary

This page defines standardized performance budgets and canonical service profiles for model endpoints served by Redwood Inference. The goal is to ensure predictable latency, availability, and unit cost across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments while providing concrete measurement and rollout guidance that engineering teams can adopt.

Goals
- Provide a small set of service profiles that cover the majority of production workloads (interactive chat, embeddings, and batch scoring).
- Define measurable SLOs (p50/p95/p99), throughput targets, and cost budgets so product and infra decisions have concrete tradeoffs.
- Specify telemetry, alerting thresholds, and testing procedures to validate compliance.
- Document recommended default infra configurations (GPU family, memory, batching) to guide Dedicated/private sizing.

Scope
This standard applies to all externally-facing inference endpoints (hosted API routes and internal microservices that return tokens/embeddings/labels). It does NOT cover long-running offline training jobs or dataset preprocessing pipelines.

Terminology
- SLO: Service Level Objective. Expressed as a latency percentile for successful requests.
- Performance budget: A cap on expected cost or latency footprint tied to a profile.
- Warm vs cold start: Warm is when a model VM/container is already resident and the KV cache is ready; cold start includes model load and init time.

Service profiles (canonical)
The following profiles are the canonical starting points. Teams may request a new profile if none fit their workload.

| profile_name | typical_use_cases | p50 latency | p95 latency | p99 latency | target_throughput (req/s) | budget (tokens/1k) | notes |
|--------------|-------------------|------------:|-----------:|-----------:|-------------------------:|-------------------:|-------|
| interactive-chat | low-latency chat UI, tool-calls, conversational completion | 40ms | 200ms | 400ms | 50 | $0.48 | Prefers small batch sizes (1-8), KV caching on prefix, CPU-offload if possible |
| high-throughput-embeddings | search index, semantic similarity, realtime recommendations | 20ms | 120ms | 300ms | 250 | $0.15 | High concurrency, larger batches (64-256), quantized models recommended |
| batch-scoring | nightly reranks, offline large prompts | 200ms | 800ms | 2s | 5 | $0.08 | Throughput-oriented, async APIs, large batches (256-2048) |

Notes: budgets column is illustrative unit cost per 1k tokens using typical model variants and Redwood pricing; teams must run their own calibration tests.

Recommended infra mapping (defaults)
- interactive-chat: A10G / T4 (for small models), H100 with multi-instance for LLMs >30B; concurrency 8-32 per GPU; prefer NVMe-backed local cache for KV.
- high-throughput-embeddings: T4 or A10G with 8–32 concurrency; enable int8 quantization where model accuracy tests pass.
- batch-scoring: CPU-backed or lower-cost GPUs (T4) with large batch windows; autoscaling based on queue depth.

Example service profile (YAML)
Teams should include a profile file alongside their service manifest. Example: 

service_profile: |
  name: interactive-chat
  model_family: chat-llm/*
  target_slos:
    p50_ms: 40
    p95_ms: 200
    p99_ms: 400
  batching:
    enabled: true
    max_batch_size: 8
    max_wait_ms: 8
  autoscaling:
    metric: requests_per_sec
    cooldown_seconds: 30
    min_replicas: 2
    max_replicas: 50
  infra_recommendation:
    gpu_family: A10G
    concurrency_per_gpu: 16
  cost_budget_per_1k_tokens_usd: 0.48

Instrumentation and telemetry
All endpoints must emit the following metrics (Prometheus names given as canonical):
- redwood_inference_request_latency_ms (labels: service, route, model, success) — record histogram buckets focused on low-latency: [5,10,20,50,100,200,400,800,1600]
- redwood_inference_request_count_total (labels: service, route, model, status)
- redwood_inference_batch_size (labels: service, model)
- redwood_inference_kv_cache_hit_ratio (labels: service, model)
- redwood_inference_gpu_utilization_percent (labels: host, gpu_family)

Aggregation windows and SLIs
- p50/p95/p99 SLIs must be computed from the request_latency histogram over a 5m rolling window for short-term alerts and a 30d window for monthly SLO reporting.
- For SLO breach checks, use rolling 1h evaluation for operational alerts and 28d for SLO burn rate analysis.

Alerting thresholds (operational)
- Immediate page (pager duty) if p99 latency > profile.p99 * 1.5 for 10m AND error_rate > 1% over the same window.
- Pager if queue_length > 2x target_throughput sustained for 15m.
- Pager for GPU OOMs or model load failures exceeding 3 occurrences in 1m.
- Warning (Slack) if p95 latency > profile.p95 * 1.2 for 15m.

Runbook excerpt: high p99 latency
1) Identify impacted routes and models (use trace tags: service, route, model).
2) Check recent deploys and model rollouts in Redwood Console; roll back to previous pinned version if rollout < 30% and errors observed.
3) Verify KV cache hit ratio. If hit ratio < 70% and profile depends on prefix caching, consider warming cache via synthetic warmers.
4) Examine batching configuration; if batch sizes are saturating single-GPU memory and causing queueing, reduce max_batch_size and increase replica count.
5) Escalate to runtime/infra oncall if GPU utilization > 95% for >10m or OOM patterns are present.

Performance testing and validation
- Baseline test: run a representative workload using the Redwood perf harness. Use two workloads: 1) steady-state at profile.target_throughput, 2) spike load 3x for 10 minutes.
- Required artifacts before production rollout: 1) perf report (p50/p95/p99), 2) cost estimation for steady-state 30d, 3) unit/regression tests for latency-sensitive prompt sets.
- Tools: k6 (HTTP), vegeta for throughput tests, and the Redwood perf harness (scripts/perf/run_profile.sh). Example command: 
  k6 run --vus 100 --duration 10m --out json=./k6-output.json ./scripts/k6/chat-test.js

Model-serving knobs (recommended defaults)
- Batching: prefer small max_wait_ms (5-10ms) for interactive-chat; larger windows OK for embeddings and batch.
- KV cache: always enable for conversational applications; retention TTL default 10m but tunable per use case.
- Quantization: prefer int8 for embedding models and medium-sized LLMs if eval delta < 1% on key prompts.
- Fallbacks: define at most two fallback model variants (one lower-capacity and one regional) and include automatic routing policy in the service profile.

Decision record (summary of tradeoffs)
- Decision: Standardize on percentile-based SLOs (p50/p95/p99) and three profile templates.
- Rationale: Percentiles capture both UX (p50) and tail behavior (p95/p99). A small set of profiles minimizes complexity for infra and provides clear cost/latency knobs for teams.
- Alternatives considered: per-service bespoke SLOs (rejected for operational overhead), only p99 SLO (rejected because p50 matters for interactive UX).

Change control and exceptions
- To deviate from a canonical profile, teams must file a short request in the infra exceptions tracker with the following: expected traffic shape, perf results, cost impact, and reviewer approvals from runtime and SRE.
- Exceptions are valid for 90 days and must include a re-review plan.

Ownership and contacts

- Runtime/Kernel team contact: runtime-kernel@redwood.example.com.

Appendix: Example evaluation checklist for new model
1) Run accuracy and hallucination checks against the model onboarding prompt set.
2) Run perf baseline (3 runs) at target_throughput. Collect p50/p95/p99 and memory footprints.
3) Validate cost projection using sample 30d traffic mix.
4) Confirm telemetry emits required metrics and tags.
5) Submit PR with service_profile YAML and link to perf report.
